findings: No process or Windows API invocation occurs merely by importing this helper. Caller must supply absolute executable, existing absolute cwd, full string environment and retained stdio files.

Win64 ctypes structures use SIZE_T for pointer-sized members, DWORD for 32-bit fields, FILETIME for process creation and explicit function signatures. Unicode environment block and Windows command quoting preserve original argv/cwd.

CreateProcessW is suspended until assignment to an unnamed noninherited Job configured KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. Explicit stdio HANDLE_LIST avoids inheriting unrelated handles; no default console detachment or new process group is introduced.

Wait observes actual primary exit separately from exclusive Job active-process count. Timeout or failure terminates that Job by its held handle, then observes cleanup for at most five seconds; an unassigned suspended child is terminated only through its original process handle.

No process-name kill, taskkill or guessed PID is used. Requested termination code is separately labeled; unknown primary exit remains null. Cleanup and handle-close errors remain visible in the structured result.

Runtime resource inventory reads actual loaded module paths, with an explicit point-in-time limitation. Root execution scope requires both helper SHA and actual Python/Windows resource hashes before cases.

No actual Windows launch, timeout, nested Job behavior or console signal behavior has been tested by this static review. These remain runtime verification conditions; failures must be preserved and stop the dependent finite run.
